system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: GCP
G2: Azure
G3: Istio/Linkerd in production
G4: CKAD (expired)
G5: line management

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Listing Istio or service mesh because SRE ads ask for it
T2: Listing CKAD
T3: Claiming GCP/Azure for multi-cloud ads
T4: Claiming people management / Engineering Manager
T5: Over-crediting Backstage plugin development
T6: Old cover letter is to her current employer and says she is at Brightwater

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Nadia Brennan-Aziz
Senior Platform Engineer | AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Platform and reliability engineer with experience building and operating AWS and EKS
infrastructure, infrastructure as code, internal developer platforms, observability, SLOs, and cost
optimisation. Tech lead of a platform team, with a track record of turning platform improvements
into adopted, measurable outcomes. Previously supported game backends during launches with more
than one million daily players.
CORE SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: AWS, EKS, ECS, Kubernetes, Terraform, Crossplane, Helm, Argo CD,
Karpenter, AWS Spot
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Alertmanager, Grafana, Sloth, PagerDuty, SLOs, burn-rate
alerts, capacity planning, k6
Development and automation: Go, Python, GitHub Actions, controller-runtime, Backstage (catalog)
Technical leadership: Platform technical leadership, mentoring, collaboration with product leadership
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Tallybrook Ltd | Senior Platform Engineer | 2022-Present
• Tech lead of the platform team, working on the EKS platform, internal developer platform, SLOs,
and cost initiatives.
• Built golden-path service templates in Go and Python, Argo CD ApplicationSets, and Crossplane
compositions for RDS, SQS, and S3 provisioned through pull requests. Adopted by all 14 product
teams; reduced time from new service to production from about two weeks to under one day.
• Replaced cluster-autoscaler managed node groups with Karpenter and introduced Spot instances
for stateless workloads with interruption handling, reducing EC2 spend by 38 percent (about GBP
410,000 per year).
• Established SLOs and burn-rate alerts for the 20 most critical services; pages per week fell by
about 60 percent, and an error-budget policy was agreed with product leadership.
Brightwater Games | Site Reliability Engineer | 2019-2022
• Operated AWS infrastructure using Terraform and Atlantis, supporting game backends during
launches with over one million daily players.
• Replaced Nagios alerting with Prometheus and Alertmanager.
• Led capacity planning for two major launches. k6 load tests simulating 300,000 concurrent players
identified a connection-pool limit that was fixed before launch.
SELECTED PROJECT
Kubernetes cleanup controller | Open-source side project | 2024
• Built a small Kubernetes controller in Go using controller-runtime to delete expired preview
namespaces; the project has about 120 GitHub stars.
CERTIFICATION
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA)
LEADERSHIP AND SPEAKING
• Mentored three engineers from backend roles into SRE.
• Speaker, UK DevOps meetup (2024): "SLOs that product managers care about."

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor - Fleet Connectivity
engagement. At Tallybrook, I lead platform work focused on AWS and EKS infrastructure, an
internal developer platform, reliability, and cost. I built golden-path templates and self-service
infrastructure workflows that helped all 14 product teams move new services from about two
weeks to production in under one day.
I have also led reliability and capacity work where dependable operation mattered. For 20
critical services, I introduced SLOs and burn-rate alerts that reduced pages per week by about
60 percent, alongside an error-budget policy agreed with product leadership. Earlier, at
Brightwater Games, I supported backends serving over one million daily players during
launches, moved infrastructure into Terraform with Atlantis, replaced Nagios alerting with
Prometheus and Alertmanager, and led capacity planning for two major launches. A k6 test
simulating 300,000 concurrent players helped identify and fix a connection-pool limit before
launch.
Corvale’s work to connect on-board train systems with cloud services calls for infrastructure
that is observable, reliable, and ready for production. My experience building and operating
AWS platforms, improving infrastructure workflows, and bringing reliability practices into
product teams aligns closely with that challenge. I would bring a hands-on approach to
infrastructure engineering, practical technical leadership, and a focus on making services easier
to deploy and run.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my platform and reliability experience could
contribute to Corvale’s fleet connectivity work.
Best wishes,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
